reason: E1 shows that LPBF strategies can program microstructure evolution in stainless steel, supporting the general concept of thermal programming, but it does not address AlCrFeNiSi, residual stress reduction, or mechanical property improvement. E2 describes SLM for HEAs but only mentions CoCrFeMnNi and does not discuss thermal programming or residual stress control. Thus, the key premises linking thermal programming to reduced stresses and improved properties in AlCrFeNiSi lack direct evidence.
premises: LPBF processing strategies can program thermal stability and control microstructure evolution in additively manufactured alloys.
In situ thermal programming (modulating laser power, scan strategies, dwell times) can moderate melt pool thermal profiles and reduce thermal gradients.
Reduced thermal gradients lead to more homogeneous solidification and lower residual stresses.
Lower residual stresses and homogeneous microstructure improve mechanical properties.
These LPBF control strategies are applicable to high-entropy alloys like AlCrFeNiSi.
